answer: In an agent marketplace, willow, jade and zephyr must each escrow collateral equal to twice the value of every job they accept. Payment and collateral stay locked until a verifiable result is delivered; a missed deadline forfeits collateral to the buyer. New identities get no unsecured credit, so splitting into a thousand agents creates no free capacity: an attacker must lock twice the total value of its concurrent jobs and loses that capital on defaults.
